headline: Approved $336,400 Page Park Phase 3 contract and 7.5 acres on Perkins Street side of Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve.
summary: The meeting covered updates on the Chippanee Golf Course and City Cemeteries acquisitions, the ADA Audit, and the FY 27 budget. Members approved the Page Park Phase 3 contract, the 7.5 acres on the Perkins Street side of Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve, the Kern Park 319 Grant MOU, and tree replanting on Veterans Memorial Boulevard. City Council will vote on purchasing Chippanee Golf Course at a special meeting on September 22, 2026.
decisions: Endorsed the Rockwell Park Stone House Rain Garden project by Eagle Scout Candidate Evan Mastripiero, all in favor.
Approved the Consent Agenda, including the minutes and the Superintendent's Report, all in favor.
Approved the Deputy Tree Warden's recommendation to remove and replant dead and dying Boulevard Pine Oak Trees on Veterans Memorial Boulevard, all in favor.
Approved the Kern Park 319 Grant MOU, all in favor.
Approved the Page Park Phase 3 contract services with Weston and Sampson in the amount of $336,400, all in favor.
Approved the acceptance of 7.5 acres on the Perkins Street side of Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve, all in favor.
Approved the Community Engagement Hearings on the ADA Audit and Transition Plan for October 20, 2026, at the Senior Center and October 21, 2026, at City Hall, all in favor.

MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Deputy Tree Warden's recommendations to remove and replant dead and dying Boulevard Pine Oak Trees on Veterans Memorial Boulevard. Seconded by Commissioner Weber; all in favor; motion carried.
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Metzroth to approve the Kern Park 319 Grant MOU. Seconded by Commissioner Donovan; all in favor; motion carried.

MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Page Park Phase 3 Contract Services to Weston and Sampson in the amount of $336,400. Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the 7.5 acres on the Perkins Street side of Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve. Seconded by Commissioner Metzroth; all in favor; motion carried.

MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Community Engagement Hearings for the ADA Audit and Transition Plan on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, from 1:00 p.m. - 2:30 p.m. at the Senior Center and Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in City Hall Council Chambers. Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.

plain_text:
City of Bristol 
Board of Park Commissioners 
 
INFORMATION TO ACCESS MEETING 
https://bristolct-gov.zoom.us/j/88962098471?pwd=tUIEr2YCTI5twlitd8mgsAnQheYx9p.1  
 
Ladies and Gentlemen: 
 
The regular meeting was held on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 6:00 PM in Meeting 
Room 1-2 in City Hall, 111 North Main Street, Bristol, CT 06010. 
 
 
1. Call to Order 
City Council Liaison Mark Dickau called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
 a. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
 
 
 b. Attendance 
 
 
Members Present: Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Chair 
Jonathan Bradley, Commissioner 
Cynthia Donovan, Commissioner 
Julie Metzroth, Commissioner 
Stacey Rudnick, Commissioner 
Aaron Weber, Commissioner 
Mark Dickau, City Council Liaison 
Dr. Joshua Medeiros, Superintendent, 
Bristol Parks, Recreation, Youth and 
Community Services 
Sarah Larson, Deputy Superintendent, 
Bristol Parks, Recreation, Youth and 
Community Services  
  
Absent:  Robert Fiorito, Vice Chair 
 
 
 None.
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to move New Business Item a. up on the 
agenda.  
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.  
 
a. Presentation from Eagle Scout Candidate Evan Mastripiero, Troop 
425, on Rockwell Park Stone House Rain Garden 
 Eagle Scout candidate Evan Mastripiero of Troop 425 presented the Rockwell Park Stone 
House Rain Garden project. Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to endorse the Rockwell Park Stone House 
Rain Garden project by Eagle Scout Candidate Evan Mastripiero. 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried. 
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Metzroth to return to the regular agenda. 
Seconded by Commissioner Weber; all in favor; motion carried. 
3. Consent Agenda 
City Council Liaison Mark Dickau presented the following items on the Consent 
Agenda. Discussion followed.  
a. Approval of Minutes 
b. Superintendent's Report 
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Consent Agenda. 
Seconded by Commissioner Metzroth; all in favor; motion carried.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to move New Business Item e. up on 
the agenda. 
Seconded by Metzroth; all in favor; motion carried.  
 e. Approve the recommendation from the Deputy Tree Warden to remove and 
replant dead and dying Boulevard Pin Oak Trees on the Veterans Memorial 
Boulevard 
 Veterans Committee Liaison John Lodivico presented the Deputy Tree Warden's 
recommendations to remove and replant dead and dying Boulevard Pine Oak Trees on 
Veterans Memorial Boulevard. Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Deputy Tree Warden's 
recommendations to remove and replant dead and dying Boulevard Pine Oak Trees on 
Veterans Memorial Boulevard. 
Seconded by Commissioner Weber; all in favor; motion carried.
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to move New Business Item b. up on the 
agenda. 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.  
b. Presentation from Pequabuck River Watershed Association on the 
Kern Park 319 Grant and approval of grant MOU 
 Mary Rydingsward of the Pequabuck River Watershed Association presented updates on 
the Kern Park 319 Grant. Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Metzroth to approve the Kern Park 319 Grant MOU.  
Seconded by Commissioner Donovan; all in favor; motion carried.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to return to the regular agenda. 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.  
4. Old Business 
 
 a. Annual Policy Review: Bristol Parks, Recreation, Youth and Community 
Services: Policies 
 Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented the annual policy review. Discussion 
followed.  
 
 b. Update on the acquisition of the City Cemeteries 
 Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented an update on the City Cemeteries acquisition. 
Discussion followed.   
 
 c. Update on the acquisition of the Chippanee Golf Course 
 Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented an update on the acquisition of Chippanee 
Golf Course. After the public forum, City Council will hold a special meeting on September 
22, 2026, to vote on purchasing Chippanee Golf Course. Discussion followed.  
 
 d. By Commissioners 
 None. 
 
5. New Business
c. Approval of Page Park Phase 3 Contract Services to Weston and Sampson in 
the amount of $336,400 and consider an additional package of $11,000,000 to 
include turf field and associated amenities 
 Superintendent Joshua Mederios and Jonathan Tunsky, Senior Project Manager at 
Weston and Sampson, presented details of the services under the Page Park Phase 3 
Contract. Superintendent Medeiros and Senior Project Manager Tunsky presented an 
additional package for a turf field and associated amenities. Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Page Park Phase 3 Contract 
Services to Weston and Sampson in the amount of $336,400. 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried. 
 
 d. Referral for the acceptance of 7.5 acres on Perkins Street side of Hoppers-
Birge Pond Preserve 
 Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu presented an overview of the 7.5 acres on the Perkins Street 
side of the Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve. Accepting the 7.5 acres would create a buffer, 
add acreage to the Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve, and require the city to pay only for the 
appraisal. Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the 7.5 acres on the Perkins 
Street side of Hoppers-Birge Pond Preserve. 
Seconded by Commissioner Metzroth; all in favor; motion carried.   
 
 f. Set the Community Engagement Hearings for the ADA Audit and Transition 
Plan for Tuesday, October 20th, 1:00 p.m.-2:30 p.m. at the Senior Center and 
Wednesday, October 21st, at 6:00 p.m. at City Hall 
 Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented the results of the ADA Audit completed by the 
WT Group AEC and presented the dates for two Community Engagement meetings. 
Discussion followed.  
 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to approve the Community Engagement 
Hearings for the ADA Audit and Transition Plan on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, from 1:00 
p.m. - 2:30 p.m. at the Senior Center and Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. in 
City Hall Council Chambers. 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradley; all in favor; motion carried.  
 
 g. Review of Current Parks Board Committees and discussion on skills and 
interests 
 Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented the current Parks Board Committees. The 
commissioners shared their personal and professional skills and interests and which 
committee best fit them. Discussion followed.   
 
 h. Preliminary FY 27 Budget Brainstorm Workshop
Superintendent Joshua Medeiros presented the results of the preliminary FY 27 budget 
workshop from the department’s all-staff meeting. During the workshop, the Bristol Parks, 
Recreation, Youth and Community Services Department identified its top priorities. Discussion 
followed.   
 
 i. By Commissioners 
 Commissioner Donovan inquired about possibly planting fruit trees in the parks in the 
future. Discussion followed. 
 
Commissioner Metzroth discussed future collaborations with other departments and 
expressed interest in helping with those partnerships. Discussion followed.  
 
6. Reports and Committee Reports 
 
 a. Fund Development & Advocacy Committee 
 Nothing to report.  
 
 b. Policy & Strategy Committee 
 Nothing to report.  
 
 c. Finance Committee  
 Nothing to report.  
 
 d. City Council Liaison Report 
 City Council Liaison Mark Dickau presented the recurring issues involving the homeless 
population at Federal Hill Green and Bracket Park. Discussion followed. 
 
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu discussed Connecticut e-bike laws and would like to discuss 
them further at a later date. Discussion followed.   
 
7. Adjournment 
MOTION: Made by Commissioner Donovan to adjourn at 7:47 p.m. 
Seconded by Commissioner Metzroth; all in favor; motion carried.  
  
Respectfully Submitted,  
Amaris Estrada 
Recording Secretary 
Board of Park Commissioners
